hints: Look first at the C=O group in each skeleton and decide if it is at the end of the chain or in the middle.
Remember that an aldehyde has -CHO at C1 while a ketone has C-CO-C, so sort 1 to 4 into aldehydes and ketones.
Check for a carbon with four different groups attached to test for chirality, then match which pair differs in functional group but both are chiral.
walkthrough:
**Identify the functional group in each structure**

Each structure contains one C=O. If it is at the end with H attached it is an aldehyde, if it is in the middle it is a ketone.

$$1: \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CHO (hexanal, aldehyde)}$$ $$2: \text{CH}_3\text{COCH(CH}_3\text{)CH}_2\text{CH}_3 \text{(3-methylpentan-2-one, ketone)}$$

**Identify 3 and 4 in the same way**

Draw out the carbon skeletons carefully from the line formulas.

$$3: \text{OHCCH(CH}_3\text{)CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3 \text{(2-methylpentanal, aldehyde)}$$ $$4: \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3 \text{(hexan-3-one, ketone)}$$

**Test for chiral centres**

A chiral centre is a carbon with four different groups. Look for a branched carbon attached to H.

$$2: \text{C3 attached to H, CH}_3, \text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3, \text{COCH}_3 \text{, chiral}$$ $$3: \text{C2 attached to H, CH}_3, \text{CHO, CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3 \text{, chiral}$$ 
1 is straight chain hexanal with no branched carbon, and 4 is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$ with no carbon bearing four different groups, so neither is chiral.

**Apply isomer definitions to conclude**

Aldehyde versus ketone is a change of functional group. Same functional group with different branching is chain isomerism.

2 (ketone) and 3 (aldehyde) are functional group isomers of each other, and both have a chiral centre as shown above. This matches the correct statement.

options.A: 1 and 3 are both aldehydes, hexanal and 2-methylpentanal. They do show chain isomerism because one is straight and one is branched, but they cannot be positional isomers because the -CHO group must be at C1 in both.
options.B: 2 is a ketone and 3 is an aldehyde, so they are functional group isomers. C3 in 2 and C2 in 3 each carry H plus three different carbon groups, so both molecules have a chiral centre.
options.C: 1 (aldehyde) and 4 (ketone) are indeed functional group isomers, but the second part fails. Neither hexanal nor hexan-3-one has a carbon with four different groups, so neither has a chiral centre.
options.D: 2 and 4 are both ketones, so they cannot be functional group isomers of each other. They differ in carbon skeleton and position of C=O, but functional group isomerism is false so the whole statement is false.
